title: Pages, slotted pages, and record layout

blocks.text: Storage managers read and write **pages** (typically 4–16 KB) — the unit of I/O between disk and memory. A **slotted page** keeps a header with a directory of record offsets, so records can be inserted, deleted, and grow in place without rewriting the page.

Everything faster in a DBMS is a story about avoiding random I/O: indexes collapse searches into a few page reads, buffer managers bet on which page will be needed next, and slotted pages make updates cheap enough to stay inside one page most of the time.

blocks.prompt: Buffer management reuses the same victim-selection logic as virtual memory — practice it through page replacement.
